question: Does an empirical detectability model built from real, unenriched shotgun data agree in direction with this tree's theoretical detectability rule (length 7-30, <=2 missed cleavages), and does it add real predictive power beyond the rule's own two ingredients?

dataset.role: Dataset B, downloaded and probed in Phase 1

protein_universe: FASTA accessions in (peptides_Global.txt non-reverse/non-contaminant 'Leading razor protein' set) UNION (proteinGroups_ABE.txt non-reverse/non-contaminant 'Protein IDs' set)
theoretical_detectable_rule: length >= 7 and length <= 30 (missed_cleavages <= 2 already holds for every generated candidate, see docstring)
target: EMPIRICAL_DETECTED = exact (protein accession, 1-based start position, sequence) match against a non-reverse, non-contaminant row of peptides_Global.txt

D1_length_direction.rule: mean EMPIRICAL_DETECTED[length in 7..30] - mean EMPIRICAL_DETECTED[length > 30]; protein-clustered bootstrap 95% CI must exclude 0 and be positive

D3_informativeness.rule: AUC(M3) - AUC(M2), per-fold then averaged; protein-clustered bootstrap 95% CI must exclude 0 and be positive; point estimate >= 0.03

D4_theoretical_flag_coefficient_sign.rule: in M3 refit with an added THEORETICAL_DETECTABLE indicator feature, its coefficient must be > 0

pass_rule: D1 and D2 and D3 and D4 all hold
